instruction: Apply orange color, bold formatting, and underlining to the titles on slides 1, 4, and 5.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing title color to orange (RGB 255,140,0) and applying both bold and underline formatting in slides 1, 4, and 5 (0-indexed: 0, 3, 4). Evaluator reads the presentation file and checks if the title text formatting matches the expected color, bold, and underline properties. Partial credit is given per slide: each slide contributes equally to the final score.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: orange color (RGB 255,140,0), bold formatting, and underline formatting on slides 1, 4, and 5 (0-indexed: 0, 3, 4)
Getter extracts the correct state: reads presentation file and extracts title formatting (color, bold, underline) from specified slides
Metric correctly compares extracted formatting against expected values using proper tuple comparison for color and boolean checks for bold/underline
Data flow is correct: getter returns dict mapping slide_idx to formatting info, metric receives rules dict directly from get_rule() and processes it correctly
Postconfig appropriately saves the file (Ctrl+S) before verification, ensuring the modified presentation is persisted to disk for reading
Partial credit logic is sensible: scores each slide individually then averages, allowing partial success if only some slides are formatted correctly
Expected values are semantically correct: RGB (255, 140, 0) is orange, slide indices [0, 3, 4] correctly map to 1-indexed [1, 4, 5] from instruction
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Title detection uses heuristic of 'first text shape with content', which may not work if slides have non-standard layouts (e.g., subtitle before title). Consider using placeholder type checking (e.g., shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE) for more robust title identification

Minor: Getter only checks first run of first paragraph for formatting. If title has mixed formatting across runs, only the first run's formatting is captured. Consider checking if all runs have consistent formatting or aggregating formatting across all runs in the title
